title: Ben Thigpen, his son Edmund, and Sonny Payne
summary: Jones discusses Ben Thigpen and his drummer son, his own son's dancing, and tells Sonny Payne to learn touch from his father.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: What about Ben Thigpen? please. please.

Ben was with Andy Kirk, of course, beautiful man. He had a son Edmund... Incidentally, Edmund thinks of me, sent me a card I didn't know that Edmund was going to play drums, you see, until later on he took me out on a tennis court. I went to St. Louis before he went into the Army. I said, "Where's the best drummer in St. Louis?" And the boys in the car said, "You just took him home." I said, "Edmund plays drums? Ben's son?" Like father, like son. He never said nothing about drums; he never talked drums, to me.
Your son plays drums. Jonathan, Jr.
He was a dancer first. You know he did Carnegie Hall; he was a dancer.
Then there a few sons of great drummers, of great fathers.
The Count Basie band has a drummer -
Son of a great father, Sonny Payne, and his father was who?
Chris Columbo. I told him, why don't you go to your father and learn some touch? 'Cause I used to see Sonny walking down Seventh Avenue. He had met Chick Webb.
